Question: Does an organised trauma system reduce mortality or improve survival among injured patients relative to usual care at 6 to 9 years of follow-up?

Study context:
Study S1
Study label: He 2016
Article ID: ART_00938
Citation: He JC, Kreiner LA, Sajankila N, Allen DL, Claridge JA. Performance of a regional trauma network: a statewide analysis. Journal of Trauma and Acute Care Surgery 2016;81(1):190-5.

outcomes:
Two analyses were done for the post-NOTS period:

1. A county analysis, comparing Cuyahoga County, the county containing NOTS L1TC, with other counties containing L1TCs.
2. A regional analysis, comparing the NOTS region with other Ohio regions with L1TC coverage.

Both the county and regional analyses showed the overall NOTS patients were 1 to 4 years older (p < 0.05), had similar or higher Injury Severity Score (p < 0.05), and were treated more often at lower-level TCs (p < 0.001). County analysis demonstrated that Cuyahoga County had approximately 1% lower mortality in geriatrics patients than non-NOTS counties. Regional analysis showed lower mortality in the NOTS region for the overall patient group and geriatric and blunt injuries subgroups. Cuyahoga was the only county that decreased mortality for both the general and groups over time (all p < 0.05).

**Outcome variables:** comparison of, demography (age/sex), treatment location (proportion of patients per TCs) and mechanism of injury (blunt, penetrating, burns, asphyxia), trauma incident per location and mortality.

results:
Effect measure: change in level
Unit: mortality cases per quarter
Polarity: lower favors intervention
Comparator effect: 0.0
Effect estimate: -2.02
Confidence interval begin: -3.17
Confidence interval end: -0.86
Confidence interval percentage: 95
Sample size: 20357

Question: Does an organised trauma system reduce mortality or improve survival among injured patients relative to usual care at 6 to 9 years of follow-up?

Study context:
Study S1
Study label: Moran 2018
Article ID: ART_00939
Citation: Moran CG, Lecky F, Bouamra O, Lawrence T, Edwards A, Woodford M, et al. Changing the system – major trauma patients and their outcomes in the NHS (England). EClinicalMedicine 2018;2:13-21.

outcomes:
Study outcomes were: trends of patient's characteristics, process of care and patient outcomes such as adjusted survival rate and mortality. these included, patient flow, the evolution of consultant-led care and imaging, increase in older age of trauma admission, and establishment of newer clinical care protocols (i.e., massive transfusion protocols and tranexamic acid protocols). There were 10247 (9.2%) deaths in the 110863 patients with an ISS of 9 or more.

There were no changes in unadjusted mortality. Risk-adjusted survival showed a 19% (95% CI 3%-36%) increase in the case-mix adjusted odds of survival in severe injury over the 9-year study period. Interrupted time series analysis showed a significant positive change in the slope after the intervention time point of April 2012 (+0.08% excess survivors per quarter, p = 0.023), i.e., an increase of 0.08 more survivors per 100 patients every quarter.

**Patient characteristic trends:** demography (age, sex etc.), injury severity (ISS), mechanism of injury (penetrating/blunt, falls) and comorbidities.

**Process of care:** time to arrival to ED, time to intubation at ED, Consultant led care at ED, time to Blood transfusion, time to surgery, percentage admitted to ICU, length of stay in hospital/ICU.

Unit: survival cases per quarter
Polarity: higher favors intervention
